newsitem.title: USA: Economist Bergsten sees dollar overvalued to yen.
newsitem.headline: Economist Bergsten sees dollar overvalued to yen.

text.p: The dollar is substantially overvalued against the Japanese yen, although its sharp rise appears to have been halted by the Group of Seven industrialized nations, trade expert Fred Bergsten said on Wednesday.

The equilibrium level of the dollar and the yen "is a considerably stronger yen that we now have," Bergsten, director of the Institute for International Economics, said at a meeting of the National Association of Business Economists here.

The G-7's statement last month, intended to halt the dollar's rise, has been succesful despite there being no evidence of direct government intervention in the currency markets, said Bergsten, a former Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for International Affairs.
Bergsten also said he agreed with the views of an earlier speaker concerning the dollar-yen relationship.
Donald Fites, chairman and CEO of Caterpillar Inc, told the same group earlier that the dollar ought to drop from its current value of about 122 yen to 100 yen.

"A yen-dollar relationship of 100 to one is much more attuned to the underlying economic conditions than the current relationship," Fites said. About half of Caterpillar's sales came from outside the United States last year, Fites said.
Criticizing the Clinton administration for talking up the dollar's value, Fites said "at some point enough of a good thing is too much."
